title: Ahrefs vs FullStory: SEO research and competitor analysis or digital experience analytics and session replay?
description: A practical decision guide for teams weighing Ahrefs against FullStory. Ahrefs focuses on SEO research and competitor analysis, while FullStory focuses on digital experience analytics and session replay. Use the workflow criteria below to decide whether you need one, the other, or both; verify current vendor capabilities, terms, and pricing before committing.

features.name: Core task
features.tool1Detail: Use Ahrefs to investigate search visibility and competitors; define the keyword or backlink questions the team needs answered and validate the data scope.
features.tool2: Digital experience analytics and session replay
features.tool2Detail: Use FullStory to investigate user journeys and interaction problems; test replay usefulness, event capture, privacy masking, and how findings connect to product changes.

features.name: Selection test
features.tool1: Run Ahrefs through a representative task and document results, setup effort, and gaps.
features.tool1Detail: Confirm must-have requirements before evaluating plans or switching tools.
features.tool2: Run FullStory through the same decision process.
features.tool2Detail: Check whether it solves the same requirement or a separate one.

features.name: Operational checks
features.tool1: Verify integrations, permissions, data handling, support, and who will maintain the workflow.
features.tool1Detail: Use vendor documentation and a small pilot; do not infer capabilities from a generic feature checklist.
features.tool2: Verify integrations, permissions, data handling, support, and who will maintain the workflow.
features.tool2Detail: Estimate total cost from current plans and actual usage, not an unverified headline price.

features.name: Relationship
features.tool1: Search performance research versus on-site experience investigation
features.tool1Detail: Do not treat either product as a universal winner; compare it with the job it is meant to do.
features.tool2: Search performance research versus on-site experience investigation
features.tool2Detail: If responsibilities are distinct, using both may make sense; confirm the handoff and avoid paying twice for the same capability.

verdict: There is no evidence-based universal winner between Ahrefs and FullStory because their primary jobs differ. Choose Ahrefs if the need described above matches your workflow; choose FullStory if its job is the one you need to solve. If both needs exist, assess whether the tools complement each other and define ownership at the handoff. Pilot the relevant workflow, verify current features and plan limits with each vendor, and compare total cost, integrations, privacy, permissions, and support before buying.

faqs.question: What is the main difference between Ahrefs and FullStory?
faqs.answer: Ahrefs focuses on SEO research and competitor analysis, while FullStory focuses on digital experience analytics and session replay. Start with the job your team needs to complete rather than comparing them as interchangeable products.

faqs.question: Can Ahrefs replace FullStory?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. A replacement only makes sense if Ahrefs demonstrably covers the requirements you currently rely on FullStory for. Test the real workflow and confirm missing integrations, controls, or outputs before switching.

faqs.question: Can a team use Ahrefs and FullStory together?
faqs.answer: Potentially, when the team needs both SEO research and competitor analysis and digital experience analytics and session replay. Define which tool owns each step, how information moves between them, and who maintains access and data quality.

faqs.question: How should I compare their costs?
faqs.answer: Check each vendor's current pricing and plan limits, then estimate total cost for the seats, usage, integrations, support, and administration required. Do not rely on stale prices or unverified rating claims.

faqs.question: What is the safest way to choose?
faqs.answer: Write down must-have outcomes, run a small pilot using a representative scenario, check security and privacy requirements, and score the results against those outcomes. Verify vendor claims directly.
